content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a polished, responsive bookmark manager.

Features include:

- Add, edit, delete, and favorite bookmarks
- Search across titles, notes, domains, and tags
- Collections with live counts
- Grid and list layouts
- Alphabetical and newest-first sorting
- Persistent browser storage
- Responsive mobile navigation
- Curated starter bookmarks and empty states

The production build and core interactions were verified in Chromium.

Open the app at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

This looks really nice — clean, and I can see my bookmarks organized into collections with search, favorites, sorting, and the grid/list views. The overall save-and-manage flow is here.

One thing matters to me for actually saving, though. When I went to add a bookmark, it asks me to type in the title (and a note) myself. What I was picturing is that I just paste the link and the app fills in the page's title and a short description for me automatically — that's really the point of saving a link for me, so I don't have to retype everything by hand. Right now every saved link would need me to write its title myself.

Can you make it so that pasting a URL pulls in the page's title and details automatically? I can still tweak them afterward, but I'd like it to start from what the page actually is. Once that's working the way I add links, I think this is basically what I wanted.

content:
Automatic link details are now working.

When you paste a URL, Gather now:

- Fetches the page title and description
- Shows loading and success feedback
- Keeps generated details fully editable
- Handles pages without metadata gracefully
- Blocks private/local network URLs for safety

Verified with a live MDN page: both its title and description populated automatically, could be edited, and saved correctly.

Try it at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

That's exactly what I was after. I pasted a link and it pulled in the page's title and description on its own, and I could still edit them before saving. Combined with everything else — organizing into collections, favorites, search, sorting, and the different views — this does what I wanted: I can easily save links and keep them managed without retyping everything by hand.

I'm happy with this. Thank you.
